name: The Gentle King Library
description: Public domain Puritan and confessionally Reformed works, gathered for gentleking.org.
rights: Every work here is in the public domain in the United States. The books marked as from CCEL are the typed texts of the Christian Classics Ethereal Library (ccel.org), shared here by its permission. Project Gutenberg books keep the Gutenberg license inside them. The King James Version and the Berean Standard Bible are the public domain editions published by eBible.org, and the translators of the Berean Standard Bible gave it to the public domain in 2023. The works marked as from the Internet Archive are kept only as links to scans of the printing named.
paths: Every path is relative to this file's folder.

works.title: The Creeds of Christendom, Volume 1: The History of Creeds
works.author: Philip Schaff
works.edition: The Creeds of Christendom, with a History and Critical Notes. New York: Harper & Brothers, 1877. Volume I: The History of Creeds.

files.label: Volume 1: The History of Creeds
files.contents: The history of creeds: a doctrinal history of the Church as set out in its public standards. It covers the ecumenical creeds, the Greek and Roman creeds (with the Vatican Council and papal infallibility), the Lutheran and Reformed (Zwinglian and Calvinistic) confessions, the Anglican articles, the Westminster Assembly and Standards, and later Protestant creeds. Index to vol. I.

works.blurb: Schaff's doctrinal history of the church's creeds, from the ancient ecumenical symbols through Roman, Lutheran, Reformed, and later Protestant confessions.

works.title: The Creeds of Christendom, Volume 3: The Evangelical Protestant Creeds
works.author: Philip Schaff
works.edition: The Creeds of Christendom, with a History and Critical Notes. New York: Harper & Brothers, 1877. Volume III: The Evangelical Protestant Creeds, with Translations.

files.label: Volume 3: The Evangelical Protestant Creeds
files.contents: The Evangelical Protestant creeds in their original languages, with English translations. Lutheran: Augsburg Confession, Luther's Small Catechism, Formula of Concord, Saxon Visitation Articles. Reformed: Zwingli's Sixty-seven Articles, Ten Theses of Berne, First and Second Helvetic Confessions, Heidelberg Catechism, Gallican and Belgic Confessions, First and Second Scotch Confessions, Thirty-Nine Articles, Anglican Catechism, Lambeth and Irish Articles, Arminian Articles, Canons of Dort, Westminster Confession and Shorter Catechism. Modern Protestant creeds: Savoy Declaration, Baptist Confession of 1688, Waldensian Confession, Methodist Articles, Evangelical Alliance, and others. Index.

works.title: A Body of Practical Divinity
works.author: Thomas Watson
works.edition: Glasgow: Blackie & Son, 1859. A Body of Practical Divinity, in a series of sermons on the Shorter Catechism of the Westminster Assembly, to which are appended select sermons on various subjects, together with The Art of Divine Contentment and Christ's Various Fulness

links.contents: The whole work in one volume. It has the preface 'To the Reader' and a short account of the author, then the sermons on the Shorter Catechism, including the Ten Commandments and the Lord's Prayer (to p. 544, 'End of the author's lectures on the catechism'). Then come seven select sermons (Sermon VI, on Col. 3:11 'Christ is all in all', is Christ's Various Fulness), The Art of Divine Contentment (pp. 609-654), The Preciousness of the Soul, The Soul's Malady and Cure, The Beauty of Grace, and The Trees of Righteousness Blossoming (to p. 688), and finally Blackie's advertisements.

works.blurb: Watson's plain, quotable sermons through the Shorter Catechism, a whole course of doctrine for ordinary Christians, with The Art of Divine Contentment.
